generations.name: C7
generations.title: Reads what the failure says
generations.summary: Before it asks a model where to look, C7 ranks your files by what the failure itself names: the files the failing tests executed, test names that match module names, and the class names in the error text. It then makes sure the top files are actually read. (A fourth step, module paths in the error text, only recognises its two development repositories' package names and does not fire on yours.)
generations.evidence: SR7, a preregistered and sealed study (2026-09-25): on 54 unseen tasks in two Python repositories, C7 repaired 57 of 162 attempts (54 tasks, 3 rounds each) against its predecessor B's 35 of 162 with the same small model (p = 0.00085), with no more errors or false fixes and about half the time per successful repair.
generations.caveat: C7 was proven against B, not against the shipped g0, on synthetic single-line bugs with one model (gpt-oss-20b). Which of its steps carried the gain was not tested. On your work it must win an online trial before it becomes active.
generations.authored_by: Runesmith's Kaizen loop, with Claude Opus 4.5 as the author instrument
